content: Data on the implementation of the recommendations at the country and regional levels will be collected and evaluated in the short to medium term by the WHO Department of Sexual and Reproductive Health and Research and the WHO Department of Maternal, Newborn, Child, and Adolescent Health and Ageing. This evaluation aims to assess the impact of these recommendations on the national policies of individual WHO Member States. Interrupted time series, clinical audits, or criterion-based audits may be employed to gather relevant data on the use of interventions outlined in this guideline. For the prevention of postpartum hemorrhage (PPH), the WHO recommends using the coverage of prophylactic uterotonics as a process indicator to monitor and prevent PPH. The proposed prophylactic uterotonic coverage indicator is calculated as the number of women receiving prophylactic uterotonics during the third stage of labor divided by the total number of women giving birth. This indicator provides an overall assessment of adherence to the recommendations included in this guideline. In addition to this, the use of other locally agreed and more specific indicators, such as the proportion of pregnant women with intravenous (IV) access who are administered IV oxytocin after vaginal birth, may be necessary to achieve a more comprehensive evaluation of the quality of care related to PPH prevention and treatment. The WHO has developed specific guidance for evaluating the quality of care for severe maternal complications, including PPH, based on the concepts of near-miss and criterion-based clinical audits. Monitoring the quality of uterotonic drugs available in low-resource settings can assist skilled health personnel in selecting the most effective uterotonic option for PPH prevention in their specific working context. The Executive Guideline Steering Group (GSG) convenes annually to review WHO’s portfolio of maternal and perinatal health recommendations. This group helps prioritize new and existing questions for recommendation development and updating. Accordingly, this recommendation will be reviewed alongside others and prioritized as needed by the Executive GSG. If new evidence emerges that could potentially impact the current evidence base, the recommendation may be updated. If no new reports or information are identified, the recommendation may be revalidated. Following the publication and dissemination of the updated recommendation, any concerns regarding its validity should be promptly communicated to the guideline implementers, along with any plans to update the recommendation. The WHO welcomes suggestions for additional questions to be included in the updated recommendation.
